True False Check

true_false_check.Rd

Verify that the logical constants are always written in full, TRUE or FALSE, and never abbreviated as T or F, when used as values inside a function: in argument values, like f(log = T) or f(T), in condition values, like if(T) or while(T), in comparison values, like x == T (both sides), and in indexing values, like n[T]. The safer-r rule requires full logical names, because T and F can be overwritten by the user (e.g., T <- 1), contrary to TRUE and FALSE.

Warning: the function first checks that all the functions used inside x are preceded by a package attribution (like colons_check() would do): if not, an error is returned, asking to run colons_check() first (like all_args_here() does). This pre-check must pass before the T or F scanning is performed.

Usage

true_false_check(x, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")

Arguments

x

a function name, written without quotes and brackets.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A table-like text message indicating the T or F symbols that must be written TRUE or FALSE or a message saying that everything seems fine.

Table-like: column 1, the line number in the function code (starting at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines); column 2, the symbol (T or F); column 3, the code preceding the symbol.

Details

The result is used to modify the code inside the tested function like this: replace T by TRUE and F by FALSE.

More precisely, true_false_check() reports every symbol T or F used as a value (see the @description section), but not the symbols used as names, because these are user-defined objects: definition target, like T <- 1, T = 1 or y -> T; assignment value, like x <- T or T -> x (deliberately not reported, because such a symbol refers to a user-defined object); formal name, like function(T); named-argument name, like f(T = 1); component after $ or slot after @, like df$T or df@F; loop variable, like for(T in 1:3); function name, like T(); help topic, like ?T, ?(T), ?((T)) or ??T, at any parenthesis depth; formula symbol, like y ~ T, T ~ y or y ~ x + T, wherever it is located in the formula.

If a name T or F is defined anywhere in the checked function code (formal name, loop variable, definition target), then all the value usages of this symbol are not reported, whatever the position in the code.

The verification is performed on the R parser output (base::parse() + utils::getParseData()), so that strings (like "T"), comments and backquoted names (like `T`) are never reported. Contrary to curl_bracket_check(), function bodies reduced to a single .Primitive(...) call do not need to be skipped, because such bodies do not contain any T or F symbol.

The package-association pre-check verifies that all the functions called with brackets (like mean()) in the code of the tested function are preceded by :: or :::. Like colons_check(), it does not check function names written without brackets, like in the FUN argument of some functions, e.g., sapply(1:3, FUN = as.character), and function names preceded by $ are not considered. Contrary to colons_check(), the pre-check is performed on the R parser output, and functions without any function call (like function(x){ x == TRUE }) are accepted, instead of returning the colons_check() "EMPTY OF FUNCTION" error. Functions like base::mean (body made of UseMethod(...)) can never pass the pre-check, exactly like they never pass colons_check(). Warning: internal functions defined with the arrow writing function(...) -> name are not detected by the pre-check (the detection only supports name <- function(...) and name <- utils::getFromNamespace(...)), exactly like in colons_check() where the arrow writing is also flagged: please, use the standard writing.

Warning: true_false_check() cannot check symbols written with backquotes, like `T`. Please, use the standard writing.

The returned line numbers are indicative, depending on which source is checked. For instance, saferDev::colons_check (compiled) has not the same line numbers as its source file. Notably, compiled functions do not have comments anymore, compared to the same source function sourced into the working environment. In addition, the counting starts at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines potentially present in source files.

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/true_false_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ if(x > 1){ base::return(TRUE) } }
saferDev::true_false_check(fun1)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::true_false_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
fun2 <- function(x){ if(x == T){ base::return(x) } }
saferDev::true_false_check(fun2)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME SYMBOLS T OR F MUST BE WRITTEN TRUE OR FALSE:
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 3	T		if (x == T) {
#> 
fun3 <- function(x){ x } # no function call: accepted by the package-association pre-check
saferDev::true_false_check(fun3)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::true_false_check().
#> INSIDE fun3(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#>
